title: IP Administrator (Experienced)
description:
IP Administrator (Experienced)
Sheffield

About Us

Withers & Rogers is one of Europe's largest dedicated intellectual property law firms, with offices across the UK, Paris and Munich. Established more than 140 years ago, we remain as passionate as ever about making intellectual property work to our clients' best advantage. Today, our clients include many renowned, innovative organisations from across Europe, North America, and Asia.

We believe that our patent and trade mark attorneys, support, and operations staff have a breadth of expertise and a depth of specialist sector knowledge that is second to none. Our purpose is building trusting relationships, and our vision is to be an independent, responsible, sustainably profitable, and globally focused firm.

The Role

This is a full-time, permanent position, and the successful candidate will be aligned to our Sheffield office. Hybrid working options, including working from home, are available.

In this role, your responsibilities will include:
- Managing own and team inboxes, processing emails and post (mainly electronic but some hard copy), updating our case management system and acknowledging receipt, where appropriate.
- Accurate and daily maintenance of the case management system, including following workflows and generating standard correspondence from templates, and liaising with Records and Finance departments, as well as sister company Withers & Rogers Renewals.
- Full secretarial support, including all typing of documents such as letters, emails, and patent specifications.
- Preparation of official forms for UK, European and other patent applications, and design applications, including use of online filing software, the payment of official fees and reporting accurately.
- Organising and prioritising own workload and keeping a level-headed approach in a busy working environment.
- Accurately following Withers & Rogers processes and procedures, and client-specific processes and procedures where applicable.
- Producing/maintaining documentation to capture processes developed for key clients.
- Accurate preparation and processing of invoices, using e-billing systems where necessary.

About You

To join us as an IP Administrator, you'll need:
- Patent administration experience is required.
- Good communication skills and ability to interact with all levels of internal and external contacts.
- Attention to detail and pride in work product.
- The ability to balance and prioritise workload, remain composed and level-headed during periods of particularly busy activity, and proactively help other members of the team.
- The ability to manage an attorney's emails, judge urgency, and act as required.
- Good Microsoft package skills, particularly Outlook, Word, Teams and Excel, with ideally an understanding of case management systems and experience in following/generating standard procedures and templates for repeat tasks.
- The desire to learn and a willingness to become involved.
- The ability to work individually and within a team.

Your Rewards
- Competitive salary
- Benefits such as a healthcare cash plan and an additional holiday purchase scheme
- Flexible working options
- Enhanced Parental Leave options
- Positive and welcoming work environment

Applications will be reviewed as they are received, so early applications are encouraged.

We foster a supportive and inclusive culture where employees are encouraged to broaden their knowledge, challenge themselves and share their ideas.

If you think you have the skills to succeed, we would love to hear from you.
working_arrangement_evidence: Hybrid working options, including working from home, are available.

title: Matter Administrator
description:
About the Role

The Matter Administrator role is a key position within the wider Finance function of a leading professional services organisation. This is a fast-paced, dynamic role that continues to evolve in response to business and client requirements.
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
- Maintaining client and matter data integrity within the organisation's billing system, including hourly charge-out rates for fee earners.
- Reviewing and validating new client and matter requests against Risk & Compliance, Finance and client-specific requirements, ensuring accurate and timely entry into the billing system.
- Prioritising multiple workstreams through a ticketing system to ensure team and business Service Level Agreements (SLAs) are consistently met.
- Liaising with Partners, Fee Earners and Finance teams across international offices to support a seamless process from client and matter inception through to billing and cash collection.
- Supporting the Commercial Finance team by maintaining agreed pricing arrangements with key clients, implementing annual rate increases to support profitability and processing any necessary reversals where increases are not accepted.
- Collaborating with internal data management teams to identify, cleanse and correct historic inaccuracies and duplicate records within the billing system. What's in it for you?
- Competitive basic salary (reviewed annually)
- Flexible, hybrid working policy
- Generous bonus scheme
- Up to 25 days holiday (rising to 28 days with service)
- Holiday exchange scheme
- Private medical insurance
- Enhanced parental leave
- Reasonable adjustments and accommodation for disabled talent in accordance with the Equality Act 2010.

title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Job Description

We are looking for an enthusiastic and highly motivated Customer Service Advisor (Also known locally as a Property Manager) to complement our Property Management Team within our Lettings Department in Sheffield. As a Customer Service Advisor you will provide property management and tenancy support services to branches, landlords and tenants.

Salary £25,000

What's in it for you as a Customer Service Advisor?
- Get full training and development
- A good understanding of the residential lettings industry
- Fast paced, fun environment
- Regular team meetings
- Full company briefings
- A career pathway

Key responsibilities of a Customer Service Advisor.
- Act as a central point of contact managing the effective resolution of queries from clients and colleagues
- Coordinating urgent and routine repairs and maintenance
- Liaising with trades people/contractors and keeping customers up to date
- Organising safety inspections and managing remedial works
- Liaising with landlords following regular property visits
- Assisting customers with general tenancy queries
- Carrying out weekly partnership calls with colleagues and welcome calls with new customers
- Dealing promptly and courteously to communication with landlord, tenants, contractors, and internal partners
- Providing a first-class service to maximise customer retention
- Ensuring personal and team deadlines are met, service levels maintained and KPI's achieved

Skills and Experience required to be successful as a Customer Service Advisor.
- Strong customer service skills and confident communicator
- Good team player
- Ability to stay calm under pressure
- Excellent negotiation and influencing skills
- Excellent planning and organisational skills
- Good analytical ability

Benefits
- Aviva Digi care + workplace / Car leasing and cycle to work scheme
- Colleague discount scheme / Perks at work / Gym discounts
- Life assurance / Workplace pension scheme
- 23 days annual leave, increasing with length of service (and your birthday off)

Connells Group UK is an equal opportunities employer and positively encourages applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of , race, disability, age, sexual orientation, transgender status, religion or belief, marital status, or pregnancy and maternity.

Don't meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and people of colour are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Connells Group we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace. So, if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't fit perfectly with every aspect of the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other opportunities.

title: Personal Injury Legal Assistant
description:
Role: Personal Injury Legal Assistant
Location: Sheffield, South Yorkshire
Contract: Full time, permanent
Salary: £24,000 - £26,000

CRA Consulting is pleased to be working alongside a leading claimant law firm in Sheffield to recruit a Personal Injury Legal Assistant to join its growing team.

This is a great opportunity for someone with experience in Personal Injury, legal administration or paralegal work who is looking to develop their technical knowledge and take on greater responsibility within a busy claimant environment.
The role will initially involve supporting the team across a range of Personal Injury matters, with the opportunity to transition into Data Breach and GDPR-related claims as your experience develops.

The Role
As a Legal Assistant, you will be hands-on with live matters and closely involved in progressing claims from initial instruction through to resolution. You'll work alongside experienced fee earners and solicitors, gaining exposure to the wider claims process and taking on increasing responsibility as you develop.
Your duties will include:
- Assisting with the day-to-day progression of Personal Injury claims
- Liaising with clients, insurers, medical professionals and other third parties
- Preparing and reviewing legal documentation and correspondence
- Obtaining and reviewing supporting evidence and medical records
- Assisting with drafting statements and other case documentation
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date case records
- Managing key dates, deadlines and ongoing case actions
- Supporting fee earners with the progression of litigated and pre-litigation matters
- Developing an understanding of Data Breach and GDPR claims, with a view to transitioning into this area of work
- Taking on increased responsibility for your own caseload as your knowledge and confidence develops

Progression into Data Breach
A key part of the opportunity is the genuine progression into Data Breach work.
You'll receive support and training to develop your understanding of claims arising from data breaches and GDPR infringements, including the impact these incidents can have on individuals. The Legal Assistants within the team are very involved in the progression of matters, so this is much more than a traditional administrative support role.

Over time, there is the opportunity to take on more responsibility and develop your own expertise within this specialist area.
About You
The firm is open to candidates from a range of backgrounds, but you are likely to have:
- Previous experience within a legal environment
- Ideally, some exposure to Personal Injury, claimant work or litigation
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- The ability to manage a busy workload and work to deadlines
- A genuine interest in developing your legal knowledge and taking on greater responsibility
- A proactive and client-focused approach

This could suit an experienced Legal Assistant, Paralegal or Personal Injury support professional who is looking for a role offering hands-on experience, specialist training and genuine career progression.
The Opportunity

You'll be joining an established team in Sheffield with the opportunity to build on your existing legal experience and develop specialist knowledge in an area of growing importance.
For the right person, this role offers a clear route from Personal Injury Legal Assistant into specialist Data Breach work, with increasing responsibility and opportunities to progress within the team.

title: Audience Development Coordinator - Local Authority - Libraries
description:
Audience Development Coordinator
- Hourly Rate: £15.56 PAYE
- Location: Central Sheffield
- Job Type: Hybrid (office and home working)

Join Sheffield Libraries as an Audience Development Coordinator and play a key role in bringing a vibrant programme of events and activities to life. This position offers a unique opportunity to engage with the community through a variety of events, from author talks to large-scale activities like Comic Fest and the Summer Reading Challenge.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Plan and coordinate a diverse range of events across Sheffield's libraries.
- Develop creative ideas for future events and activities.
- Support the execution of events such as author talks, history talks, re-enactments, Comic Fest, and the Summer Reading Challenge.
- Organise the upcoming Book Awards.
- Handle event administration and complete relevant forms.
- Coordinate payments for external contributors and suppliers.
- Promote library events through social media and create newsletters to showcase upcoming activities.
- Attend events to ensure smooth operation, meet and greet the public, authors, speakers, and other guests.
- Introduce authors and speakers at events as required.
- Conduct outreach and networking to develop relationships with individuals, groups, and organisations.
- Collaborate closely with colleagues and different teams across the library service.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Friendly, enthusiastic, and approachable demeanor.
- Creative mindset with a knack for suggesting innovative ideas.
- Highly organised with strong coordination skills.
- Confident in communicating with a diverse range of people.
- Experienced in delivering excellent customer service.
- Skilled in networking and building new relationships.
- Comfortable supporting or hosting public events.
- Proficient in using social media and creating promotional content.
- Able to balance creative initiatives with established processes and procedures.
- Capable of working both independently and as part of a team.
- Experience in events, community engagement, audience development, or related fields is advantageous.

Benefits:
- Flexible hybrid working arrangement, with approximately three office days per week.
- Opportunity to work on engaging and diverse events.
- Chance to meet a wide variety of people and make a significant impact in the community.
- Competitive hourly rate and time off in lieu (TOIL) for occasional evening or weekend work.
- Saturday overtime paid at time and a half.

How to apply:

If you're an organised, creative, and confident communicator who enjoys events and engaging with people, apply today to become part of Sheffield Libraries. Please submit your CV and a cover letter detailing your relevant experience and why you are interested in this position.

title: Call Centre Operator
description:
Sales Advisors

If you're outgoing, full of energy and love talking to people, you'd be better off in sales with EE.

Maybe you've worked in retail, or hospitality before. You know how to deal with customers but you're looking for something more exciting - a job that's going to challenge you. And, of course, you want to earn a bit more cash.

Our Doncaster team's full of people like you - so you'll be in great company here.

What does being a sales advisor involve?

You'll join a lively sales team in our Doncaster contact centre. We'll train you to take incoming calls from existing EE customers and help them find the best deals on their phones and broadband. You'll also help them to navigate the different tech products we sell.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE

GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.

UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.

BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.

GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.

FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.

GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

You need to be a great listener as well as a fluent talker. A lot of the time, you'll pick up on something that someone has said, then use that to match them with the perfect product.

Forget what you've heard about sales

Don't let what you've heard about sales put you off. Let's smash a few myths
- Yes, there are targets to hit. But the kind of people who like sales, love that. You're probably naturally competitive. You get a buzz out of beating the person next to you. You hate being bored at work.
- It's not "cold calling". The calls come in to you and you decide how best you can help the customer. That's why we value resourceful people who like fixing problems.
- People say it's "hard selling". It's really not! You're basically talking to people about fun tech stuff that they already want. Who doesn't love a better phone, faster broadband or a new console?

Why you'll be better off at EE

GREAT MONEY - you start on £26,116 which goes up to £26,738 after 8 months.

UNCAPPED COMMISSION - the more you sell, the more you can earn.

BRILLIANT BENEFITS - including 24/7 GP appointments for you and your family, free parking and discounts on EE products like phones and broadband that could save you £100s every year.

GROWTH - we're passionate about developing our people. There are plenty of career paths across EE and BT.

FLEXIBILITY - you can bank hours then take time off when you need. Plus, generous leave for carers and anyone starting a family.

GREAT PEOPLE - you're working with people like you. It's a sociable, supportive environment.

title: Payroll Administrator - Accountancy Practice
description:
Are you an experienced Payroll Administrator, Payroll Executive or Payroll Officer currently working within an accountancy practice or payroll bureau and looking for a role where you can take ownership of your own client portfolio?

We are working with a highly established and rapidly growing accountancy and business advisory group that is looking to strengthen its Rotherham payroll team with an experienced payroll professional.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a sizeable and ambitious firm at an exciting stage of its development. The wider group employs around 300 people, with the Rotherham office currently home to approximately 25 staff and set to grow significantly to circa 40 staff over the next few months.

The Rotherham office acts as an important payroll hub for the wider business, supporting clients across Rotherham, Sheffield and other offices within the group.

THE ROLE

You will take responsibility for managing your own portfolio of payroll clients, typically consisting of around 50-100 clients, ranging from small owner-managed businesses through to larger employers with approximately 200 employees.

This is a varied, payroll position requiring strong organisational skills, accuracy and the ability to manage multiple payroll deadlines.

Responsibilities are expected to include:

Managing a portfolio of weekly, fortnightly and monthly payrolls
Processing payroll from start to finish for a broad range of clients
Processing starters, leavers, salary amendments, bonuses, overtime and other payroll changes
Calculating statutory payments including SSP, SMP, SPP and other statutory leave
Processing PAYE, National Insurance and pension deductions
Completing RTI submissions to HMRC
Managing auto-enrolment and workplace pension requirements
Producing payslips, payroll reports and associated client documentation
Processing year-end payroll requirements, including P60s and other statutory reporting
Liaising directly with clients regarding payroll queries and information requirements
Ensuring payrolls are completed accurately and within agreed deadlines
Maintaining compliance with current payroll legislation and HMRC requirements
Supporting the on-boarding of new payroll clients where required
Resolving payroll discrepancies and more detailed client queries
Working closely with colleagues across payroll, accounts and the wider practice

ABOUT YOU

We are particularly interested in hearing from candidates who already have experience working within an accountancy practice, payroll bureau or outsourced payroll environment.

You are likely to have:

Previous experience managing multiple client payrolls
Experience working across weekly, fortnightly and monthly payroll cycles
Confidence managing your own portfolio and deadlines
Strong knowledge of PAYE, National Insurance and statutory payments
Good understanding of auto-enrolment and workplace pensions
Experience completing RTI submissions
Strong attention to detail and accuracy
The confidence to deal directly with clients and resolve payroll queries
The ability to prioritise a busy workload across multiple payroll deadlines

Experience using BrightPay would be highly advantageous, although candidates with strong experience of other payroll systems will also be considered.

A CIPP qualification would be beneficial but is not essential. Candidates who are interested in studying towards CIPP may also be supported with their professional development.

THE TEAM

You will join an established payroll function within the Rotherham office, working alongside experienced payroll colleagues as well as wider accounts and business advisory teams.

Rotherham is one of the groups larger offices and acts as a central point for payroll services across a number of locations.

The firm continues to grow through both organic development and acquisition, providing excellent long-term opportunities for someone who wants to build their career within a substantial and progressive accountancy group.

There may occasionally be opportunities to visit other offices within the group for training or team development.

WHAT'S ON OFFER?

Salary of £30,000 - £36,000, depending on experience
37.5 hour working week
Free on-site parking
Additional parking available in a nearby multi-storey
Established and supportive payroll team
Ownership of your own client portfolio
Exposure to a broad mix of clients and payroll sizes
Support towards CIPP development where appropriate
Opportunity to join a growing regional accountancy group
Long-term career development within an expanding business

The role is predominantly office based in Rotherham, although the firm can offer flexibility as and when required.

If you are an experienced payroll professional currently working within practice or bureau and are looking for a stable, varied role within a growing firm, I would be very interested in speaking with you.

Apply now for a confidential discussion about the opportunity.

Butler Rose is committed to equality in the workplace and is an equal opportunity employer.
Butler Rose Ltd is acting as an Employment Business in relation to this vacancy.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Working within the Reward team, the Payroll Administrator will support the delivery of the payroll for the various legal entities in Klipboard. As the payroll administrator, you will play a crucial role in managing and administering payroll and pension processes. Your primary responsibility will be to ensure accurate and timely processing of payroll, compliance with statutory regulations, and efficient administration of pension schemes. This role requires a deep understanding of UK payroll and pension regulations, strong attention to detail, and excellent organizational skills

Key Responsibilities:
- Process and coordinate monthly payroll activities, ensuring all payroll inputs are accurately captured, including new starters, leavers, contractual changes, sickness, maternity, paternity, overtime, and shift payments.
- Administer statutory payments and entitlements, including SSP, SMP, and SPP, and provide employees with guidance on eligibility and benefits.
- Conduct payroll reconciliations and validation checks to ensure payroll accuracy, completeness, and compliance with statutory requirements.
- Maintain accurate payroll, pension, benefits, and employee records across payroll and HR systems.
- Calculate and process salary increases, overtime payments, shift allowances, and other pay adjustments in accordance with company policies and contractual requirements.
- Prepare and deliver payroll-related reports, analysis, and management information to support HR, Finance, and business requirements.
- Reconcile and maintain data between payroll, HRIS, pension, and other related systems to ensure consistency and accuracy.
- Prepare and submit payroll information and statutory reports to HMRC, pension providers, and other relevant bodies in line with reporting requirements.
- Administer pension schemes and employee benefit programmes, including enrolment, contribution management, and query resolution.
- Monitor, investigate, and resolve payroll audit exceptions, discrepancies, and data anomalies in a timely manner.
- Ensure all payroll transactions are processed in compliance with payroll legislation, tax regulations, National Insurance requirements, and company policies.
- Act as a key point of contact for employees, providing clear and accurate advice on payroll, taxation, pensions, benefits, and related queries.
- Support internal and external payroll, pension, and compliance audits, ensuring accurate documentation and audit trails are maintained.
- Collaborate closely with HR, Finance, pension providers, and external stakeholders to ensure efficient payroll operations and regulatory compliance.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of payroll, taxation, pension, and employment legislation to ensure ongoing compliance and best practice.
- Identify opportunities to improve payroll processes, controls, reporting, and service delivery, contributing to continuous improvement initiatives.
- Support compliance inspections, PAYE reviews, pension audits, and other regulatory requirements as necessary.
- Undertake additional payroll, reporting, and administrative responsibilities as required in line with the scope and level of the role.

Skills, Knowledge and Experience:
- Strong numeracy and high attention to detail
- Competence with and experience of payroll systems and procedures.
- A strong eye for detail with an innate desire for accuracy
- Proficient in effective collaboration with internal and external stakeholders
- Ability to take responsibility for own work.
- Ability to maintain absolute discretion and maturity in handling sensitive/confidential data.
- Excellent time management skills with a proven ability to meet tight deadlines.
- High standards of work and performance.
- Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite to include intermediate Excel skills (Pivot Tables,
- V-Lookups, etc.)
- Effective team player with a 'can do' attitude.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Company Info

You may also have seen from our recent posts that we are excited to begin sharing our new company name - Klipboard. Kerridge Commercial Systems (KCS) is becoming Klipboard and our new brand is designed to bring together our expertise across distribution, automotive, retail, rental, transport management, manufacturing, and field service management. We have offices based across the world and we are looking for talented individuals to join our growing teams. Due to our growth over the last few years it is an exciting time to join us as we enter our next chapter!

Equal Opportunities

As a global company, we value and respect the diversity of our workforce, aiming to empower everyone to embrace each other's differences. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where diversity, equity, and inclusion are integral to our company and culture. We recognize the benefits of a diverse workforce, where creativity and valuing differences enable us all to thrive and sparks innovation.

This is a busy and varied role providing administrative support to the Medical Undergraduate Team and wider Medical Education Team. You will help coordinate education and training for medical students, resident doctors and other learners, including teaching programmes, placements, inductions, examinations and educational events. As a key point of contact for learners, faculty and external partners, you will maintain accurate records, respond to enquiries, support meetings, coordinate rooms and resources, collect feedback and use departmental systems. We are looking for someone who is organised, accurate, a confident communicator and able to manage competing priorities while contributing positively to a busy team. The role is predominantly based within the Medical Education Centre, with occasional attendance at other locations within South Yorkshire. Join us and play an important part in supporting the next generation of doctors. The Medical Education Administrator plays an important role in helping us provide a welcoming, organised and positive educational experience for medical students, resident doctors and other learners. We are looking for someone who enjoys working with people, takes pride in delivering a high-quality service and can bring enthusiasm, flexibility and attention to detail to a busy team. You will need to be approachable and professional, with good communication and organisational skills and the confidence to manage changing priorities. Medical Education is a varied and rewarding environment where no two days are quite the same. You will work with learners at different stages of their careers and alongside colleagues who are passionate about supporting education, training and development. In return, you will join a friendly and supportive team where your contribution is valued and where you will have opportunities to develop your knowledge, skills and experience. If you enjoy working as part of a team, building positive working relationships and knowing that your work contributes to the development of our future medical workforce, we would love to hear from you Please see attached the job description and person specification for the full details about the role and the responsibilities
